rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: A view attributed to al-Farra takes the sky as splitting open over a white cloud.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تتشقق السماء عن الغمام الأبيض عن الفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky splits so the angels can descend, as the verse itself says.
rows.anchor: وإنما تتشقق السماء لنزول الملائكة وهو قوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The inhabitants of each successively opened heaven descend, and each heaven has more inhabitants than the one below it and more than earthly jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: تتشقق السماء الدنيا فينزل أهلها وهم أكثر ممن في الأرض من الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day true sovereignty belongs to the Merciful, while the dominion of all other kings disappears.
rows.anchor: الملك الذي هو الملك حقا ملك الرحمن يوم القيامة ويزول ملك سائر الملوك فيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Kingship has three forms: divine majesty, religious authority granted by God, and coercive rule gained by force.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الملك ثلاثة أضرب ملك عظمة وهو لله تعالى وحده وملك ديانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day is exceptionally hard for unbelievers but as easy for believers as the least difficult prayer they performed in worldly life; this is glad tidings for believers.
rows.anchor: ويهون على المؤمنين كأدنى الصلاة صلوها في دار الدنيا وفي هذا بشارة للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The regretful wrongdoer who bites his hands is identified as ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عقبة بن أبي معيط بن أمية بن عبد شمس على ما مضى ذكره عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the scene applies generally to every wrongdoer regretful on Judgment Day and every friend who befriends another outside God's cause.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عام في كل ظالم نادم يوم القيامة وكل خليل يخال غيره في غير ذات الله

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: The wrongdoer eats his hands to the elbows; they regrow, and he repeatedly eats them again in remorse.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: يأكل يديه حتى تذهبا إلى المرفقين ثم تنبتان ولا يزال هكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regretful speaker wishes he had followed Muhammad and taken a path with him toward guidance.
rows.anchor: أي ليتني اتبعت محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم واتخذت معه سبيلا إلى الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unnamed former friend is identified as Ubayy.
rows.anchor: { يا ويلتي ليتني لم أتخذ فلانا } يعني أبيا { خليلا }

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the former friend as Satan; under the general reading, it means any friend who misleads from religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد به الشيطان عن مجاهد وإن قلنا إن المراد بالظالم هنا جنس الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite name فلانا covers every misleading companion; listing Pharaoh, Haman, Iblis, and other misleaders would have been lengthy.
rows.anchor: ولو قال لما اتخذ فرعون وهامان وإبليس وجميع المضلين لطال فقال فلانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The friend diverted and turned the speaker away from the Reminder, meaning the Qur'an and faith in it, after it came through the Messenger.
rows.anchor: أي عن القرآن والإيمان به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan abandons a person in the Hereafter, handing him to destruction without being able to help him.
rows.anchor: لأنه يتبرأ منه في الآخرة ويسلمه إلى الهلاك ولا يغني عنه شيئا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Muhammad complains that his people abandoned both the Qur'an and him and denied them.
rows.anchor: يعني هجروا القرآن وهجروني وكذبوني عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the Qur'an abandoned means leaving it unread and not trying to understand it.
rows.anchor: والمعنى جعلوه متروكا لا يسمعونه ولا يتفهمونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poetic example shows that وقال الرسول can mean “the Messenger says”: the past-form ما وزنوا has the present sense ما يزنون.
rows.anchor: لو يوزنون بزف الريش ما وزنوا أي ما يزنون

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A polytheist would worship a stone idol, then discard it and worship a better-looking one when he saw it.
rows.anchor: وكان الرجل من المشركين يعبد الحجر والصنم فإذا رأى أحسن منه رمى به وأخذه يعبد الآخر عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: The person abandons worship of the Creator and makes a stone his god; this is reported from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: من ترك عبادة خالقه وإلهه هو حجر فعبده ما حاله عندك عن عطاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Following and obeying one's desire makes it like a god, while the person abandons the truth.
rows.anchor: من أطاع هواه واتبعه فهو كالإله له وترك الحق عن القتيبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet cannot act as guardian to protect such a person from following desire and worshipping what he desires.
rows.anchor: لأن الوكيل هو الكافي للشيء ولا يكون كذلك إلا وهو قادر عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question asks whether Muhammad can guide someone who neither reflects nor considers; he cannot, since a guardian must be capable of what he undertakes.
rows.anchor: أتقدر أنت يا محمد أن تهديه إذا لم يتدبر ولم يتفكر أي لا تقدر على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not hear with a learner's intent or reason through Muhammad's recitation and the miracles and proofs they witness.
rows.anchor: ما يعاينونه من المعجزات والحجج أي لا تظن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are like livestock, which hear a call but do not understand it.
rows.anchor: أي ما هم إلا كالبهائم التي تسمع النداء ولا تعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are worse than livestock because people were enabled to know the truth but failed to know it, unlike animals.
rows.anchor: من الأنعام لأنهم مكنوا من المعرفة فلم يعرفوا والأنعام لم يمكنوا منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock are instinctively guided away from harm, whereas people know the ways of ruin and salvation yet pursue ruin and shun salvation.
rows.anchor: ولأن الأنعام ألهمت منافعها ومضارها فهي لا تفعل ما يضرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address “Have you not seen?” is directed to the Prophet but intended for all morally responsible people.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد به سائر المكلفين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The phrase asks the listener to see what the Lord did, with “the Lord” understood by deleting a genitive construction.
rows.anchor: أي ألم تر إلى فعل ربك ثم حذف المضاف عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Alternatively, “see” means know, as an act of inward perception.
rows.anchor: معناه ألم تعلم فيكون من رؤية القلب عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The shadow is extended from dawn until sunrise, with this explanation also reported from al-Dahhak and Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
rows.anchor: من وقت طلوع الفجر إلى طلوع الشمس عن ابن عباس والضحاك وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shadow is called extended because no sun accompanies it, as the shade of Paradise is likewise described as extended without a sun.
rows.anchor: وجعله ممدودا لأنه لا شمس معه كما قيل في ظل الجنة ممدودا إذ لم تكن معه الشمس

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Shadow is what the sun effaces in the morning; fayʾ is what the sun effaces after noon, named for its turn from east to west.
rows.anchor: الظل ما نسخته الشمس وهو بالغداة والفيء ما نسخ الشمس وهو بعد زوال الشمس

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: A preceding interpretation cites Hud 11:92 as a parallel for taking something behind one's back, and identifies “the unbeliever” as Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: واتخذتموه وراءكم ظهريا [هود: 92] والأول أوجه وقالوا عنى بالكافر أبا جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent to give glad tidings of Paradise and warn of the Fire.
rows.anchor: من النار وقد سبق معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad asks no payment for the Qur'an or conveying revelation; whoever wishes may spend wealth in obedience to God and seek His approval.
rows.anchor: أي على القرآن وتبليغ الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He seeks no personal wage but encourages spending for God's approval; this confirms his honesty, since a demand for payment would invite the charge that he seeks their wealth.
rows.anchor: إني لا أسألكم لنفسي أجرا ولكني لا أمنع من إنفاق المال في طلب مرضاة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entrust affairs to the Ever-Living, who will vindicate the Prophet even after time has passed and cannot let vengeance escape Him.
rows.anchor: فوض أمورك إليه فإنه ينتقم لك ولو بعد حين فإنه الحي الذي لا يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Glorify with praise” means praising God while declaring Him free of attributes that cannot belong to Him, with appropriate words of gratitude.
rows.anchor: أحمده منزها له عما لا يجوز عليه في صفاته بأن تقول الحمد لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command means worship and pray to God in thanks for His favors.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وأعبده وصل له شكرا منك له على نعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fully knows His servants' sins and will reckon and recompense them, so they should fear and watch Him.
rows.anchor: عليما فيحاسبهم ويجازيهم بها فحقيق بهم أن يخافوه ويراقبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What is between them” refers to what lies between the categories of heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: أي ما بين هذين الصنفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about God's establishing Himself upon the Throne was explained earlier in the commentary on al-Aʿraf.
rows.anchor: قد سبق تفسيره في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: “Ask an expert about Him” takes the preposition باء to mean “about”; the expert is God.
rows.anchor: فاسأل عنه خبيرا والباء بمعنى عن والخبير ههنا هو الله تعالى عن ابن جريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alqamah's poetry illustrates باء serving in place of عن.
rows.anchor: وأنشد في قيام الباء مقام عن قول علقمة بن عبدة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the expert is Muhammad, whom people should ask about God because he knows Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الخبير هنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والمعنى يسأل كل منكم عن الله تعالى محمدا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, باء retains its basic sense: ask a knowledgeable person who can tell you the truth about God's attributes.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الباء على أصلها والمعنى فاسأل بسؤالك أيها الإنسان خبيرا يخبرك بالحق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another usage is like “I met a lion in so-and-so,” describing the person's bravery; seeing him is like seeing the comparison, so ask him about God as one who knows Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الباء في قولك لقيت بفلان ليثا

rows.speaker: نفطويه
rows.claim: After Jews recounted a creation account that contradicted revelation, God says to ask Him; by asking, one is asking an expert.
rows.anchor: وروي أن اليهود حكوا عن ابتداء خلق الأشياء بخلاف ما أخبر الله تعالى عنه فقال سبحانه فاسأل به خبيرا قال نفطويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “What is the Merciful?” asks what sort of thing He is and reflects their claim not to know Him.
rows.anchor: أي وأي شيء الرحمن والمعنى أنا لا نعرف الرحمن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Rahman is a divine name found in earlier scriptures, but the polytheists did not know it as God's name and had to be told it was one of His names.
rows.anchor: الرحمن اسم من أسماء الله عز اسمه مذكور في الكتب الأولى ولم يكونوا يعرفونه من أسماء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, Rahman means one possessing mercy without limit; the pattern faʿlan intensifies a quality to its utmost, as in fully sated, thirsty, joyful, or glad.
rows.anchor: لأن فعلان من أبنية المبالغة تقول رجل ريان وعطشان في النهاية من الري والعطش

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mentioning the name al-Rahman made them recoil further from faith.
rows.anchor: أي زادهم ذكر الرحمن تباعدا من الإيمان عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their aversion grew toward the truth and acceptance of the Prophet's words.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنهم ازدادوا عند ذلك نفورا عن الحق وقبول قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding discourse connects God's selection of the Messenger with his virtues, the signs that establish God's oneness and power, their rejection of clear signs, the beneficial purpose of revelation, refusal to seek payment, reliance on God, and eventual reckoning.
rows.anchor: وجه اتصال الآية بما قبلها أن فيها إخبار أنه سبحانه أفرده بالإرسال مراعاة لحسن التدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Servants of the Merciful” means His foremost servants; the possessive marks special honor and approval, like calling an obedient, approved child “my son.”
rows.anchor: يريد أفاضل عباده وهذه إضافة التخصيص والتشريف كما يقال ابني من يطيعني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: They walk calmly, with dignity and obedience, neither insolent, playful, arrogant, nor corrupt; this is also reported from Mujahid.
rows.anchor: بالسكينة والوقار والطاعة غير أشرين ولا مرحين ولا متكبرين ولا مفسدين عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: They walk according to their natural disposition, without affectation or strutting.
rows.anchor: هو الرجل يمشي بسجيته التي جبل عليها لا يتكلف ولا يتبختر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: They are forbearing and learned, not responding in ignorance even when others behave ignorantly toward them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه حلماء علماء لا يجهلون وإن جهل عليهم عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Another description is that they are chaste and God-fearing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أعفاء أتقياء عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ignorant address them with words they dislike or find burdensome, and they answer with upright speech rather than obscenity, as Mujahid explains.
rows.anchor: أي سدادا من القول لا يقابلونهم بمثل قولهم من الفحش عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, they answer with words that keep them from sin, or they simply greet the others; Qasas 28:55 is cited as evidence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سلاما أي قولا يسلمون فيه من الإثم أو سلموا عليهم دليله قوله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: They do not respond to ignorant people with ignorant behavior.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: كانوا لا يجاهلون أهل الجهل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: They do not act ignorantly alongside someone who is acting ignorantly.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لا يجهلون مع من يجهل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Their conduct by day is among people; their nights are spent in private worship, alternating between prostration and standing.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: هذه صفة نهارهم إذا انتشروا في الناس وليلهم خير ليل إذا خلوا فيما بينهم وبين ربهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Anyone who reaches night has “spent the night,” asleep or awake; here they pray at night in prostration and standing, seeking God's reward.
rows.anchor: كل من أدركه الليل فقد بات نام أو لم ينم والمعنى يبيتون لربهم بالليل في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They pray for Hell's punishment to be turned away because it is a permanent, urgent, inescapable burden.
rows.anchor: أي يدعون بهذا القول وغراما أي لازما ملحا دائما غير مفارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is a wretched place for settlement and residence.
rows.anchor: أي إن جهنم بئس موضع قرار وإقامة هي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: For Ibn Abbas and Qatadah, extravagance means spending on sins and stinginess means withholding what is due to God.
rows.anchor: فقيل هو النفقة في المعاصي والإقتار الإمساك عن حق الله تعالى عن ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi defines extravagance as exceeding the proper limit in spending and stinginess as spending less than what is necessary.
rows.anchor: وقيل: السرف مجاوزة الحد في النفقة والإقتار التقصير عما لا بد منه عن إبراهيم النخعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' chest is constricted by their denial, while his tongue fails to move because of the knot in it; speech may also fail from a tongue defect or from constriction of the chest and loss of ideas.
rows.anchor: أي لا ينبعث بالكلام للعقدة التي كانت فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks for Aaron to assist him, as one calls for help when a difficulty occurs, out of eagerness to fulfill the command.
rows.anchor: يعني ليعاونني كما يقال إذا نزلت بنا نازلة أرسلنا إليك أي لتعيننا وإنما طلب المعاونة حرصا على القيام بالطاعة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Moses would have made this request only after God permitted it, since prophets ask only what they are authorized to ask.
rows.anchor: لم يسأل موسى ع ذلك إلا بعد أن أذن الله له في ذلك لأن الأنبياء لا يسألون الله إلا ما يؤذن لهم في مسألته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “sin” Moses fears is his killing of the Copt, a killing Pharaoh's people claim was a sin against them.
rows.anchor: يعني قتل القبطي الذي قتله موسى ع أي لهم علي دعوى ذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fears they may kill him because of that history, not while delivering the message; he knows God guarantees aid to messengers in conveying it.
rows.anchor: خاف أن يقتلوه بتلك النفس لا لإبلاغ الرسالة فإنه علم أن الله تعالى إذا بعث رسولا تكفل بمعونته على تبليغ رسالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Certainly not” is a rebuke assuring Moses they will not kill him, because God will not empower them against him.
rows.anchor: وهو زجر أي لا يكون ذلك ولن يقتلوك به فإني لا أسلطهم عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron is omitted from the command “go,” but the dual form and Moses' request show that God sent Aaron with him.
rows.anchor: وحذف ذكر هارون وإجابة موسى إلى ما اقترحه من إرساله معه إلى فرعون لدلالة قوله فاذهبا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are the proofs and miracles God specially granted the two messengers.
rows.anchor: أي بدلالاتنا ومعجزاتنا التي خصصناكما بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being with them means protecting them and hearing what occurs; mustamiʿūn means sāmiʿ because listening as a sought act does not apply to God, and the wording is more emphatic.
rows.anchor: أي نحن نحفظكم ونحن سامعون ما يجري بينكم ومستمع هنا في موضع سامع لأن الاستماع طلب السمع بالإصغاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is confirmed by God's statement “I am with you both; I hear and see.”
rows.anchor: إني معكما أسمع وأرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “with you” treats the two messengers as a group.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال إنا معكم لأنه أجراهما مجرى الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron were sent by God to call Pharaoh to worship Him and abandon associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: أرسلنا الله إليك لندعوك إلى عبادته وترك الإشراك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular رسول can carry a plural sense, as a Hudhayl poem uses the expression “the best of messengers.”
rows.anchor: لأن الرسول قد يكون في معنى الجمع قال الهذلي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, رسول means “message”; a cited poetic line uses the word that way.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الرسول بمعنى الرسالة كما في قوله

rows.speaker: العباس بن مرداس
rows.claim: A poem by al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās uses the feminine رسول for رسالة; a verbal noun can serve as an adjective, and an adjective can stand in place of a verbal noun, yielding “we are bearers of the Lord of the Worlds' message.”
rows.anchor: ألا من مبلغ عني خفافا رسولا بيت أهلك منتهاها فأنث الرسول تأنيث الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to send the Israelites means release them from enslavement and let them go; the narrative compresses the fact that Moses and Aaron delivered God's message as commanded.
rows.anchor: أمرك الله بأن أرسلهم وأطلقهم من الاستعباد وخل عنهم وفي الكلام حذف تقديره أنهما أتيا فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Did we not raise you?” describes nurturing something through successive stages, meaning Pharaoh raised Moses from infancy.
rows.anchor: والتربية تنشئة الشيء حالا بعد حال معناه ألم تكن فينا صبيا صغيرا فربيناك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses lived with Pharaoh's people for eighteen years.
rows.anchor: وهي ثماني عشرة سنة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid says Moses lived with Pharaoh's people for thirty years.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ثلاثين سنة عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Moses lived with Pharaoh's people for forty years.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أربعين سنة عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh mentions raising Moses to claim credit for kindness toward him.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال ذلك امتنانا عليه بإحسانه إليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh reveals his meanness by recounting his favors.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه أظهر لؤمه حيث ذكره صنائعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deed Pharaoh mentions is Moses' killing of the Copt.
rows.anchor: { وفعلت فعلتك التي فعلت } يعني قتل القبطي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: “You were among the ungrateful” means ungrateful for Pharaoh's favor and the benefit of his upbringing; also reported from ʿAtaʾ and Muqatil.
rows.anchor: لنعمتنا وحق تربيتنا عن ابن عباس وعطاء ومقاتل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses was an unbeliever in his own deity because he had followed Pharaoh's religion before criticizing it; also reported from al-Suddi.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وأنت من الكافرين بإلهك إذ كنت معنا على ديننا الذي تعيب وتقول إنه كفر عن الحسن والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses means he acted ignorantly and did not know the blow would lead to the man's death.
rows.anchor: أي فعلت هذه الفعلة وأنا من الجاهلين لم أعلم بأنها تبلغ القتل

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Alternatively, “astray” means forgetful.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه من الناسين عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Alternatively, he did not know that his action would result in the man's death.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الضالين عن العلم بأن ذلك يؤدي إلى قتله عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, he missed the right course unintentionally, like someone aiming at a bird but hitting a person.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الضالين عن طريق الصواب لأني ما تعمدته وإنما وقع مني خطأ كمن يرمي طائرا فيصيب إنسانا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, he was astray from prophethood because revelation had not yet forbidden him to kill.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الضالين عن النبوة أي لم يوح إلي تحريم قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted Moses judgment, meaning prophethood.
rows.anchor: { فوهب لي ربي حكما } أي نبوة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, judgment is knowledge of what wisdom requires, including the Torah and knowledge of lawful and unlawful matters and other rulings.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الحكم العلم بما تدعو إليه الحكمة وهو الذي وهبه الله تعالى لموسى من التوراة والعلم بالحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Moses a prophet among the other prophets.
rows.anchor: أي نبيا من جملة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation hears Moses acknowledge that Pharaoh's upbringing was a favor, while reproaching him for enslaving Israel rather than Moses; the question is implied.
rows.anchor: أن فيه اعترافا بأن تربيته له كانت نعمة منه على موسى وإنكارا للنعمة في ترك استعباده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation denies that raising Moses was a favor, since Pharaoh enslaved Moses' people and thereby nullified any favor he claims.
rows.anchor: أنه إنكار للمنة أصلا ومعناه أتمن علي بأن ربيتني مع استعبادك قومي هذه ليست بنعمة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that without enslavement and killing Israelite sons, Moses' mother would not have cast him into the river; the claimed favor arose from Pharaoh's own oppression.
rows.anchor: أنك لو كنت لا تستعبد بني إسرائيل ولا تقتل أبناءهم لكانت أمي مستغنية عن قذفي في اليم

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari elaborates that Pharaoh's forbidden enslavement caused Moses' family to cast him into the river, so the upbringing became a favor only as a result of Pharaoh's wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: إنما صارت لك علي نعمة لما أقدمت عليه مما حظره الله عليك

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Another view says Pharaoh has no favor over Moses because his mother and fellow Israelites raised and protected him under Pharaoh's order to enslave them.
rows.anchor: أن الذي تولى تربيته أمه وغيرها من بني إسرائيل بأمر فرعون لما استعبدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh asks what kind or genus the Lord of the Worlds is, as if Moses were calling him to worship an entity of some category.
rows.anchor: أي أي جنس رب العالمين الذي تدعوني إلى عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses identifies the Lord as creator, originator, and maker of the heavens and earth and all animals, inanimate things, and plants between them.
rows.anchor: { وما بينهما } من الحيوان والجماد والنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If you are certain” may mean certain God has these qualities or certain that these things are originated, not created by the audience; whatever is originated must have an originator.
rows.anchor: بأن الرب من كان بهذه الصفة أو موقنين بأن هذه الأشياء محدثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses does not answer what genus God is, because God is not of a genus; instead he states God's lordship and attributes and proves them from creation beyond the creatures' ability.
rows.anchor: ولم يشتغل موسى لجواب ما سأله فرعون لأن الله تعالى ليس بذي جنس بل اشتغل ببيان ربوبيته وصفاته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Pharaoh's question to those around him means, “Do you not hear what Moses says?”
rows.anchor: يريد ألا تستمعون مقالة موسى عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh means, “Do you not attend to and understand what he is saying?” and expresses amazement.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ألا تصغون إليه وتفهمون ما يقوله معجبا من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh is amazed because he ignorantly asked what genus God is; if God belonged to a bodily genus, He would be originated like other bodies subject to change.
rows.anchor: لأنه طلب منه أي أجناس الأجسام هو جهلا منه بالتوحيد لأنه لو كان كأحد أجناس الأجسام لكان محدثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses points to God through the effects of His actions; Pharaoh complains that Moses answers a different question, while Moses continues gently, repeating and strengthening the proof.
rows.anchor: فقال فرعون انظروا إلى هذا أسأله عن شيء فيجيب عن غيره فجرى موسى ع على عادته في الرفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses reinforces his earlier proof: Pharaoh claimed lordship over contemporaries, but the true Lord owns and governs every generation, including earlier fathers.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكره تأييدا لما قبله وتوكيدا له فإن فرعون كان يدعي الربوبية على أهل عصره دون من قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh calls Moses mad because he answers a question about God's nature by speaking of something else.
rows.anchor: لأني أسأله عن ماهية رب العالمين فيجيبني عن غير ذلك كما يفعل المجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses does not answer the insult; he strengthens and clarifies his proof by naming the Lord of east, west, and all between them.
rows.anchor: لم يشتغل موسى ع بالجواب عما نسبه إليه من الجنون ولكن اشتغل بتأكيد الحجة والزيادة في الإبانة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, “if you reason” means knowing that only one with these attributes deserves worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن كنتم تعلمون إنه إنما يستحق العبادة من كان بهذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh threatens that anyone who takes a god other than himself will be imprisoned; they say he kept prisoners until they died.
rows.anchor: أي من المحبوسين قالوا وكان إذا سجن أحدا لم يخرجه حتى يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks whether Pharaoh would imprison him even if he brought a clear proof establishing his truth and Pharaoh's falsehood.
rows.anchor: معناه أتسجنني ولو جئتك بأمر ظاهر تعرف به صدقي وكذبك وحجة ظاهرة تدل على نبوتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqdam means what existed before another, like awwal and asbaq; qadar is existence with no beginning; tabrīz means displaying or making something manifest; ghāwī is one who acts in a way that forfeits reward; kabkabū is emphatic reduplication of kabb and means to tumble groups into Hell; ḥamīm is a beloved close friend whose affection is mutual.
rows.anchor: الأقدم الموجود قبل غيره ومثله الأول والأسبق والقدر وجود الشيء لا إلى أول والتبريز الإظهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “hear you” ordinarily takes a sound as its object; when a person is its object, it takes two objects with the second denoting audible speech or reading, never an inaudible action.
rows.anchor: هل يسمعونكم أصله أن يتعدى إلى ما كان صوتا مسموعا تقول سمعت كلامك فإن وقع على جوهر تعدى إلى مفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do they hear you when you call?” deletes the noun “your call,” as the clause “when you call” makes clear.
rows.anchor: على حذف المضاف والتقدير هل يسمعون دعاءكم فحذف المضاف ودل عليه قوله إذ تدعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception “except the Lord of the Worlds” is detached; alternatively, it is connected if the meaning is that everything worshipped is an enemy to Abraham except the Lord, despite their worshipping idols alongside Him.
rows.anchor: إلا رب العالمين استثناء منقطع ويجوز أن يكون غير منقطع على تقدير فإن جميع ما عبدتم عدو لي إلا رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “except the one who comes to God,” the noun and relative clause may be accusative as a substitute for the omitted object of “benefit”: no person, wealth, or children benefit except that person.
rows.anchor: إلا من أتى الله الموصول والصلة في محل النصب على البدل من مفعول ينفع المحذوف تقديره يوم لا ينفع أحدا مال ولا بنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the relative clause is accusative as an exception.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يكون منصوبا على الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase هم فيها is a subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: هم فيها مبتدأ وخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يختصمون may be a circumstantial accusative, or a predicate of the subject with فيها attached; on the latter analysis it is subjunctive after an implied أن in response to the wish.
rows.anchor: يختصمون في موضع نصب على الحال ويجوز أن يكون يختصمون خبر المبتدأ وفيها يتعلق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Abraham is recited to Muhammad as a forefather of the prophets and a source of Arab pride, offering him consolation and his people admonition.
rows.anchor: أي خبر إبراهيم فإنه شجرة الأنبياء وبه افتخار العرب وفيه تسلية لك وعظة لقومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham challenges his father and people by asking what they worship besides God.
rows.anchor: أي أي شيء تعبدون من دون الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Their statement that they remained devoted to idols means they kept praying to them.
rows.anchor: أي فنظل لها مصلين عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means they persisted in worshipping them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه فنقيم على عبادتها مداومين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks whether the idols hear their supplications, answer them, benefit them, or harm them if left; religion must rest on proof, or he would not have argued this way.
rows.anchor: معناه هل يستجيبون دعاءكم إذا دعوتموهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people admit they follow the practice of their forefathers, exposing their reliance on inherited imitation.
rows.anchor: وهذا إخبار عن تقليدهم آباءهم في عبادة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's challenge concerns the idols worshipped by the people and their earliest ancestors; كان appears because the statement combines the present with the past.
rows.anchor: أي والذين كان آباؤكم يعبدونهم وإنما دخل لفظة كان لأنه جمع بين الحال والماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They are enemies to me” means idolatrous worship, together with the idols, is Abraham's enemy; the masculine plural treats the idols as rational beings and likens their harm to an enemy's.
rows.anchor: إن عبادة الأصنام مع الأصنام عدو لي إلا أنه غلب ما يعقل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, “they” means the idols, given a rational masculine plural because Abraham describes them as enemies; it may also reflect that some worshipped God alongside idols, with the rational form prevailing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه يعني الأصنام وإنما قال فإنهم فجمعها جمع العقلاء لما وصفها بالعداوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception “except the Lord of the Worlds” excludes God from all those worshipped.
rows.anchor: ولذلك استثنى فقال { إلا رب العالمين } استثناء من جميع المعبودين
